items.title: Matt Shumer (@mattshumer_)
items.summary: Built a first-person destruction sandbox. Nothing in it was downloaded. Every texture is drawn to a canvas when the page loads. There isn’t a single image file in the game. The wallpaper is arithmetic. Built with @mattshumer_ ’s gauntlet loop prompt style grandmas-house-alpha.vercel.… Link EVERYTHING MUST GO She kept it all for fifty years. She is in the next room, and she can hear you. A first-person comedy destruction sim that runs in your browser. grandmas-house-alpha.vercel.app

items.title: Matt Shumer (@mattshumer_)
items.summary: Here's a car racing version using @mattshumer_ prompt! speed-racer-ten.vercel.app - You can play the game here! You can control weather, lighting. Use 'WASD' for driving and 'C' to change the camera angles. It didn't manage to one shot it after 18+ hours using Opus 5 ultracode - but with a few tweaks it did a pretty good job! I've been using this technique for the last few weeks in my independent harnesses and the build, verify, critique loops (gauntlet loops as Matt calls it) greatly have improved final outcomes of my products. Video Matt Shumer (@mattshumer_) Claude Opus 5 one-shotted this game. EVERYTHING you see in this demo is custom code... not a single external asset was used. AI games are going to be amazing. (sound on) Video — https://nitter.net/mattshumer_/status/2081054356405731740#m
